t.4.46.1: Directed by the king of the monkeys, the leaders of the monkey troops went forth swiftly in all directions, just as they had been told, for the purpose of finding Vaidehī.
t.4.46.2: They search on every side the lakes, the rivers, the thickets, the sky and the cities, as well as places made inaccessible by rivers, and the mountains.
t.4.46.3: All the leaders of the monkey troops are searching the regions described by Sugrīva, together with their mountains, woods and forests.
t.4.46.4: Having searched all day, the vānaras, all intent on finding Sītā, would gather together on the earth at nightfall.
t.4.46.5: And on every one of those days, the monkeys, having come upon fruit-laden trees that bear in all seasons in those lands, made their beds there for the night.
t.4.46.6: Counting from that day as the first, the leaders of the monkey troops, without hope, went within the month to Prasravaṇa and met with the king of the monkeys.
t.4.46.8: Then the heroic Śatabali, that great monkey, having searched the entire northern quarter, returned together with his army.
t.4.46.7: Having searched the eastern quarter as he had been instructed, together with his counsellors, but without finding Sītā, the mighty one returned, his head bowed.
t.4.46.9: Suṣeṇa, having searched the western quarter together with the monkeys, assembled when the month was complete and approached Sugrīva.
t.4.46.10: Approaching Sugrīva, who was seated with Rāma on the summit of Mount Prasravaṇa, and saluting him, they spoke these words to him.
t.4.46.11: All the mountains, the forests and the cities have been searched, as have the rivers that run down to the sea, and likewise all the countries.
t.4.46.12: All the caves that you described were searched, and the great thickets, densely overspread with creepers, were searched as well.
t.4.46.13: In dense regions, in places hard of access and rugged, creatures of enormous size were searched out and slain; and those regions that were dense with thickets were searched again and again.
t.4.46.14: That great-souled lord of the monkeys, noble in strength and lineage, will find Maithilī; for Hanūmān, the son of Vāyu, has set out toward that very quarter in which Sītā was taken.
